market_context: United States and Canada; refrigerator storage of deli meats and cold cuts, distinguishing opened packages, deli-sliced meat, and dry-cured products.
title: How Long Do Deli Meats Last in the Fridge?

seo.title: How Long Deli Meat Lasts in the Fridge
seo.meta_description: Opened deli meat and meat sliced at the deli counter generally keep 3–5 days refrigerated; unopened packages last longer. Dry-cured meats follow different rules.
seo.search_intent: Determine how long deli meats and cold cuts can be refrigerated safely and distinguish opened, unopened, sliced, and dry-cured products.

excerpt: Opened deli meat or meat sliced at the deli counter generally keeps for 3 to 5 days in a refrigerator at 40 °F or below. An unopened factory-sealed package can last about 2 weeks or until its labeled date. Dry-cured sausages and meats are different products and should be stored according to their own labels.
content_html:
The phrase “deli meat” covers foods that look similar in the refrigerator but do not always age the same way. Turkey sliced at the counter yesterday, an unopened package of ham, and a dry salami should not all get the same storage rule.

For refrigerated ready-to-eat lunch meat, the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service gives a clear baseline: 3 to 5 days after opening, or 3 to 5 days for meat sliced at a deli counter. A factory-sealed unopened package is generally listed at about 2 weeks, unless its labeled date comes first.

Start by separating moist lunch meat from dry-cured meat

If the product is moist, refrigerated, sliced, and ready to eat—turkey, bologna, cooked ham, and similar cold cuts—the short 3- to 5-day window is the relevant one after opening.

A dry sausage or heavily cured product can follow a very different storage schedule. Drying, curing, packaging, and whether the product is shelf stable all change the answer, so do not apply the deli-meat number automatically to every salami or cured sausage.

Deli-counter meat is already “opened”

Meat sliced to order no longer has the original factory seal. Treat the purchase date as day one of its short refrigerator window and label the package if you are unlikely to finish it immediately.

Keep it tightly wrapped or in a sealed container on an interior refrigerator shelf at 40 °F or below. Good packaging also helps prevent the edges from drying and keeps the meat separated from raw foods.

An unopened package does not ignore its printed date

The roughly two-week USDA guideline for unopened lunch meat is a general cold-storage reference, not permission to store a package beyond a manufacturer's more restrictive date.

Once you open it, the situation changes. A package can have a date ten days away and still be past its practical 3- to 5-day opened window.

Appearance can reject food, but it cannot prove safety

Some sliced meats develop harmless color shifts or iridescence as light reflects from muscle fibers. Color alone can therefore be misleading.

Strong off odors, a sticky or slimy surface, swelling in the package, or obvious deterioration are reasons to discard the meat. But the absence of those signs is not a reason to stretch the storage period indefinitely.

Freeze extra portions early

If you buy more deli meat than you will use in a few days, separate part of it and freeze it while it is fresh. USDA guidance uses about 1 to 2 months as a quality target for frozen lunch meat.

Small portions make thawing easier. Thaw in the refrigerator and avoid repeatedly warming and rechilling the whole package.

Higher-risk people may need extra precautions

Ready-to-eat deli meats receive special attention because of Listeria monocytogenes, particularly for pregnant people, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Anyone in a higher-risk group should follow the current public-health advice for reheating or avoiding certain refrigerated ready-to-eat meats.

The useful rule begins with the category, not the calendar. Opened or deli-sliced lunch meat: 3–5 days. Factory-sealed refrigerated lunch meat: about 2 weeks or its labeled date. Dry-cured meat: check its own storage instructions because it may follow a completely different timeline.

faq.question: How long does opened deli meat last in the fridge?
faq.answer: Generally 3–5 days at 40 °F or below, according to USDA guidance for ready-to-eat lunch meats.

faq.question: How long does deli-counter meat last?
faq.answer: Treat meat sliced at the deli counter like an opened product and use it within about 3–5 refrigerated days.

faq.question: Does unopened lunch meat last longer?
faq.answer: A factory-sealed package is generally listed at about 2 weeks, but follow any earlier use-by date or package instruction.

faq.question: Does dry salami only last 3–5 days?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Dry and cured sausages can have very different storage times, so follow the product's specific label rather than the general deli-meat rule.
